title: Leave Oncall Business trust assignment to the platform
body:
Oncall import configuration failed because its deployment specification declared the platform-assigned `RER_BUSINESS_TRUST` as an optional owner secret. Remove that declaration from the seed's packaging policy and owner-deploy input, rebuild the deployment specification, and regenerate the source lock. The runtime continues to consume the platform-provided binding.

Started at oncall-20 `6f37d0d29daaf2caedadd2b7d01d43b6fafb1e09`; current main was already an ancestor. Base main confirms the declaration was explicit Oncall policy, not a generator default.

Validation: platform main `f5bfe15adab081f8a8acda446722f8a252ce650d` passes `validateImportedSource(source,{requireSpec:true})` and `validateMailDeclaration` on the exact committed bytes. Production build, typecheck, contract and descriptor/setup/workflow generator equality, source-lock check, `rer check --profile first-party`, native replay flow (including team-manager receipts), and agent conformance (5899/5899) pass. Runtime and test files are unchanged; no local full `rer verify` was run.

Separate release follow-up: an extra direct artifact-packaging check encounters the existing missing public `MAIL_FROM` build input (`Managed mail requires one public MAIL_FROM sender, not a secret MAIL_FROM`). The same generator failure reproduces with both main's and oncall-20's packaging policies against the built Worker. This repair does not change mail policy or Base's generator.

Receipts retain binding IDs, revisions and digests without names, argument bodies or cached results. Portable export excludes them, and native subject erasure inventories and clears them atomically. The existing rer 0.2.90 adoption and current main's newer OC-033 judgment and intake tests are retained.

title: Adopt rer 0.2.90 and native erase replay; blocked on team scope
body:
Oncall now installs published npm `@runeditrun/rer@0.2.90`. Native erase classification uses installation-bound receipt custody after a completed effect, so an approved erase can replay after its target has been deleted. This draft is BLOCKED on three seed-owned team-manager replay failures outside the brief's erase-only implementation scope. It is a saved draft, not a landing candidate.

The release was checked first: `git ls-remote https://github.com/runeditrun/base 'refs/tags/rer-v0.2.90*'` peeled to `ab97e5e864013ef03fd7f1e1a335101dd9150891`; `npm view @runeditrun/rer@0.2.90 version` returned `0.2.90`. The initial live attempt-17 head was `5957bcd16fa82366e31a18a4e2a387e08da8aca8`, with main `79715c40164a4c0e65b428dee9406ef9d52a1b31` already its ancestor. A final fetch brought main `35d20dd` into this branch, retaining its newer OC-015 evidence and paging archive tests, then regenerating the adoption clauses, contract documents and source lock. Attempt 17 has since advanced with its own transfer fixture fix and remains on 0.2.89. Its branch and PR #39 are untouched.

`pnpm add -D -E @runeditrun/rer@0.2.90` and the full-SHA `rer refresh-base` succeeded. Refresh required declaring the release's `miniflare@5.20260907.0-alpha` dependency. There is no Git SHA package dependency and no supplied Base checkout. The recorded Run and contract renderer adaptations remain.

Conformance measurements:

| Source | Passed / total | Failures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.2.89 attempt-17 head, inherited report | 5886 / 5893 | Four team-manager/access-widen and three erase points |
| 0.2.90 before any erase seed change, installed `rer verify` | 5887 / 5893 | Three team-manager and three erase points |
| 0.2.90 after erase custody, installed `rer verify` and direct conformance | 5893 / 5896 | Three team-manager points |

Closed assertions: `BASE-AGENT-006.2.held.approved.access-widen` through the released replay-4 behavior; `BASE-AGENT-006.2.held.approved.erase`, `BASE-AGENT-007.5.receipt.erase`, and `BASE-AGENT-013.4.held.erase` through native erase receipt custody. Successful erase replay reaches three additional real assertions. Nothing was weakened, skipped or deleted.

Remaining failures, all **core-by-us**:

- `BASE-AGENT-006.2.held.approved.team-manager`
- `BASE-AGENT-007.5.receipt.team-manager`
- `BASE-AGENT-013.4.held.team-manager`

They reproduce both before and after the erase change. Base `modules/agent-door/pipeline.ts:121` calls the native classifier with completed effect facts, as documented by `types.ts:55-57`. Oncall `src/agent-door/management-tools.ts:90-91` ignores that completed argument and calls `current()`, whose `editTeam` call reaches `src/teams/model.ts:50` with the consumed revision. The result is `revision_conflict`. The brief expected these to clear without a seed change, but expressly permits only the erase seed change. A dated PENDING-SEED marker names this actual cause. There are no remaining failures honestly attributable to an undeclared family or a Base edge, and no 0.2.91 writer is claimed as a fix. Replay-4 is shipped and is not a pending reason. A scope decision is required before adapting team-manager.

Erase receipt custody is written in the same native erasure CAS transaction (`0155_agent_erasure_receipts.sql`). It carries binding IDs and digests for workspace, target, approval, sponsor, agent, client, consent, revision and exact arguments; it contains no erased content or cached response. Completed classification checks current native role/scopes, owner identity, agent revocation, consent, Pause and client binding before admitting that record. Base remains the sole source of replay admission and the original approval outcome. Fresh erasures retain native revision, confirmation and exact review binding. Portable export excludes the new custody; public subject erasure inventories and clears prior receipts atomically. The erasure fence is unchanged.

The inherited transfer failure was reproduced from its completed CI log: the paired-owner fixture never chose a company policy, so the machine declaration returned 403. `tests/transfer.mjs` now adopts an explicitly signed policy through the real HTTP door using its existing signer. Production authority is unchanged.

Validation:

- Installed CLI reports `0.2.90`; actual runner tooling is Node 22.20.0.
- Typecheck and production build exit 0.
- Installed `rer verify` passes the runtime journeys, hosted-output checks and hydration checks, then exits 1 solely for the three named team-manager assertions. The final main merge changes test/contract evidence only; its activation journey, regenerated clauses and browser captures are checked again on the merged source.
- `tests/oncall-agent-flow.mjs`, including the new erase helper in its existing registration, exits 0: native rollback when receipt insertion fails, held approval, equal receipt/no second effect, no retained content, and refused changed key/arguments, missing scopes, changed consent/client, revoked consent, Pause and owner demotion.
- Transfer journey exits 0: populated checkpoint and portable restore, inactive authority, native/public erasure and old-archive fences.
- Existing agent browser journey exits 0. State selectors use the release's semantic `data-approval-state` attributes instead of obsolete displayed machine codes. Pending/executed erase and unavailable approval states are included. Desktop and mobile captures have no overflow, serious/critical axe findings or undersized measured controls; personally inspected the screenshots.
- `rer check --profile first-party`, contract generator check, source lock check and `git diff --check` exit 0. `rer door clauses --write` and contract generation retain all adoption clause statuses; source lock was regenerated last. Main's OC-015 partial-to-done promotion is preserved; this adoption promotes no clause. Generated totals are 11 done, 49 partial, 41 missing (101 total).
- Setup was already declared and verified: `rer-setup.json`, sha256 `68809996abfc3689b9574c921c5880a45c8e36955b450be60aa2c761965be08a` in `rer-project.json`.

The declared capability set remains exactly `tools`, `policy`, `pause`, `audit`, `idempotency` in both `agent-surface.json` and `createAgentDoor`. Principal authorization and owner-bound tokens remain unconditional. Optional families remain unclaimed; OC-038/OC-040 remain partial and OC-074 missing. Paging remains OFF, with release 1 coordination beside the existing pager.

No deploy, release, tag, main push, workflow dispatch or rerun. The branch is saved with `[skip ci]`; no red candidate is pushed and no exact-head green Verify is claimed while the seed-owned failures remain.

title: Correct multi-character sanitization of inbound mail headers
body:
Maintenance item gr-mt-oncall-code-4: Correct multi-character sanitization of inbound mail headers

Sources: https://github.com/just-every/run-oncall/security/code-scanning/8

CodeQL alert 8 (js/incomplete-multi-character-sanitization) at headers.mjs messageIds(): the header was validated by stripping <id> tokens with replace() and checking the remainder was empty. The behaviour was already safe (any leftover, including recreated '<'/'>', failed), but the strip-and-compare pattern is what CodeQL flags. Replaced it with one anchored full-match test /^(?:<[^<>\s]+>\s*)+$/ followed by extracting the ids; no string is rewritten any more. Accepted and refused inputs are identical (checked <a@b>, folded lists, trailing junk, nested/unbalanced brackets, empty <>). Because headers.mjs is a pinned Base copy, updated its sha256 in base-copies.json and sources.lock.json (and the lock's base-copies.json hash); rer check passes. Default for owner: if Base should keep byte-exact parity, apply the same change upstream in Base. Fix round 1: the publication scan's secret.assignment at base-copies.json came from the dependencies copy: its logout.mjs digest (3bfa236e...) no longer matched the file in the tree, because an earlier maintenance commit (fd84e75) changed logout.mjs without refreshing the inventory, and one mismatched file voids the whole copy's same-tree proof. Recorded the current digest (d2760dc2...) in base-copies.json and sources.lock.json (plus the lock's base-copies.json hash). The scan now reports no secret.* finding. Remaining scan finding, not part of this fix and already on main: hygiene.email in .github/assets/media/preview.gif; default: strip the address from the gif metadata in a separate change. Removed my ignored dist/ build output.

Tests: rer check: exit 0; pnpm typecheck: exit 0; Base publication scan on the tree: no secret.* findings (only the preexisting preview.gif email hygiene finding); earlier: rer build then node tests/activation.mjs passed 19 requirement flow groups on b80f456 (this round changes only two JSON records).
